statement: Let \(f(x) = x^2 + 2007x + 1\). Prove that for every positive integer \(n\), the equation \(\underbrace{f(f(\cdots(f}_{n\text{ times}}(x))\cdots)) = 0\) has at least one real solution.
Find the number of integers \(c\) with \(-2007 \leq c \leq 2007\) such that there exists an integer \(x\) for which \(x^2 + c\) is a multiple of \(2^{2007}\).
Consider \(n\) points in the plane that are the vertices of a convex polygon. Prove that the set of lengths of the sides and diagonals of the polygon has at least \(\lfloor n/2 \rfloor\) elements.

\(2007^2\) unit squares are arranged forming a \(2007 \times 2007\) table. Arnold and Bernold play the following game: each move by Arnold consists of taking four unit squares forming a \(2 \times 2\) square; each move by Bernold consists of taking a single unit square. They alternate, with Arnold going first. When Arnold cannot make a move, Bernold takes all remaining unit squares. The player with more unit squares wins. Is it possible for Bernold to win regardless of how Arnold plays?

Let \(ABCD\) be a convex quadrilateral, \(P\) the intersection of lines \(AB\) and \(CD\), \(Q\) the intersection of lines \(AD\) and \(BC\), and \(O\) the intersection of diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\). Show that if \(\angle POQ = 90^\circ\), then \(PO\) is the bisector of \(\angle AOD\) and \(OQ\) is the bisector of \(\angle AOB\).

Given real numbers \(x_1 < x_2 < \cdots < x_n\) such that every real number occurs at most twice among the differences \(x_j - x_i\) for \(1 \leq i < j \leq n\), prove that there are at least \(\lfloor n/2 \rfloor\) real numbers that occur exactly once among such differences.
